title: A short history of the exam
text: The written examination {{1}} introduced at Cambridge in the 1790s for a practical reason: the university had grown {{2}} large for the old system, {{3}} tutors questioned each student in turn. {{4}} is the anonymous answer sheet {{5}} made mass assessment possible, and the paper exam soon spread to schools, civil services and empires. Critics {{6}} complained ever since that a three-hour sprint rewards memory over understanding, and candidates {{7}} nerves have entered legend would surely agree. Even so, nothing has replaced it for over two centuries, {{8}} everyone quietly suspects that a calm head on the day is worth more than a term of gentle coursework.

gaps.explanation: Past passive with a singular subject: was introduced.

gaps.hint: adverb: grown ___ large for the old system
gaps.explanation: 'Too large for' — the excess that forced the change.
Non-defining relative after the comma referring to the old system.

gaps.hint: cleft pronoun: ___ is the anonymous answer sheet
gaps.explanation: The cleft structure emphasises the answer sheet.

gaps.hint: relative: the answer sheet ___ made it possible
gaps.explanation: Defining subject relative with no comma; 'that' heads it.
Present perfect with a plural subject: have complained.

gaps.hint: relative: candidates ___ nerves have entered legend
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' links the candidates to their nerves.
The two clauses are added: and.
